evidence.requirements: Every requirement in the brief is met as written. The three tastings with the brief's data are in src/server/store.ts:17-21. The start page shows title, date and time, 'EUR n per guest' and '<n> seats left' (TastingList.tsx:28-33, format.ts:15; start.jpg). The link is labelled 'Book {title}' (TastingList.tsx:44). The form has fields labelled Name, Email and Guests, a 1-8 range and a 'Book' button (BookingForm.tsx:77-108, shared/api.ts:13-17). Server-side seat limit: store.ts:74-75. Errors appear under the field they concern (Field.tsx:19-23; form.jpg). The confirmation shows the heading 'Booking confirmed', tasting, guests, total and reference (Confirmation.tsx:25-34; confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a 'Sign in' button (Staff.tsx:48-58), and the password comes from STAFF_PASSWORD (index.ts:5). Bookings are grouped by tasting with name, email, guests, reference and a 'Cancel' button (Staff.tsx:100-140; staff.jpg). Cancelling frees seats because seats are derived from the bookings map (store.ts:35-40, 94-96). A fully booked state exists (TastingList.tsx:24-38, BookingForm.tsx:62-65). The layout works on a phone (agent's own 375px captures in .playwright-mcp). Built with React, Express, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind. Data is kept in memory. PORT defaults to 3000 (index.ts:4).
evidence.correctness: Seat checks are synchronous inside a single Node event-loop tick (store.ts:74-77), so concurrent requests cannot overbook. A booking for exactly the seats left is accepted and one more is rejected with 409 and a 'Only N seats left' / 'fully booked' message on the guests field (app.ts:70-75). zod rejects non-integer, 0, 9 and non-numeric guests, and coerce turns an empty value into 0, which is then rejected. Cancel deletes the booking, so seats return and the old confirmation link gives 404 (tested in api.test.ts:275-286). Minor gaps: after a 409 the booking page keeps showing the stale seats-left count, because useApi is not reloaded (BookingForm.tsx:44-48). In the staff view a non-401 failure of /api/staff/bookings renders an empty page with no error (Staff.tsx:84-100). Cancel runs immediately with no confirmation step (Staff.tsx:130-136).
evidence.security: The password is compared with timingSafeEqual over SHA-256 digests, which avoids length leaks (staff.ts:6,14). Sign-in is disabled when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset (staff.ts:9, index.ts:6). Session tokens are random 32 bytes held in a server-side map with an 8h expiry and pruning (staff.ts:17-36). The cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, and Secure behind a trusted proxy (app.ts:24-26). Sign-out invalidates the session on the server. Failed sign-ins are rate-limited (app.ts:32-39). The JSON body is capped at 10kb, x-powered-by is disabled, and the generic error handler leaks no stack traces (app.ts:136-140). Staff routes are protected by requireStaff. React handles escaping and there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. No secrets are in the code. Small gaps: there are no security headers or CSP (no helmet). The limiter keys by IP with trust proxy off by default, so behind a reverse proxy any visitor's failed attempts would lock staff out.
evidence.code_quality: Small, clearly separated modules: store.ts (domain, discriminated CreateResult union), staff.ts (auth), app.ts (HTTP), and a shared zod schema used by both client and server (shared/api.ts). The client has a reusable Field component, a small useApi hook and a format helper. Naming is clear, TypeScript is strict, and there is no needless abstraction. Error handling is explicit for 400/404/409/429 and network failure (BookingForm.tsx:40-50, api.ts:14-18). The only minor blemish is the silent empty render on a staff list fetch error.
evidence.tests: api.test.ts uses supertest against the real Express app. It covers the listing, totals, the seat decrement, the exact-boundary booking, overbooking and fully booked cases (409 with field message), seats unchanged after a rejected booking, a table of invalid inputs (empty or long name, bad or missing email, 0/9/2.5/'many' guests, no body), malformed JSON, unknown tasting and reference, cookie flags, Secure behind a proxy, a missing STAFF_PASSWORD, 8h expiry with fake timers, sign-out, rate limiting, auth on list and cancel, grouping, and that cancel frees seats. client.test.tsx tests the start page, field-level errors with accessible descriptions, the server 409 message, the confirmation flow, the network-error alert, the fully booked form, a wrong password, and staff list/cancel/sign-out. Gaps: no concurrency test, and no end-to-end test against the built server (client tests mock fetch).
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show a coherent winery look: burgundy header with a gold rule, serif headings, cream background and card layout (start.jpg). Errors are clear, with a red border and message under the field (form.jpg). The confirmation is a distinct green success card with a monospaced reference (confirmation.jpg). The staff view is a clean grouped table with a stacked card layout on mobile (staff.jpg, .playwright-mcp/kb-staff-375-v2.png). There is a fully booked state with a disabled-looking label. Weaker points: the design is fairly generic and text-only, with no imagery, description or location for guests. Staff can cancel with no confirmation. On mobile the 'Reference' label inherits the monospace font.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are tied to inputs with htmlFor/id, and errors set aria-invalid and aria-describedby (Field.tsx:9-23, tested via toHaveAccessibleDescription). The page declares html lang='en'. Headings follow a logical h1/h2 order. The staff page uses a semantic table with an sr-only 'Actions' header. Alerts use role='alert' for load/submit errors. react-hook-form moves focus to the first invalid field on client validation. Gaps: field errors coming back from the server (setError at BookingForm.tsx:46) are neither focused nor announced live. Every staff 'Cancel' button has the same accessible name, with no booking context. The gold focus ring on cream/white is low contrast. The 'No seats available' text (stone-500 on stone-100) is close to the minimum contrast.
evidence.simplicity: About 600 lines of source. Dependencies fit the problem and the brief's call for established libraries: Express, react-router, react-hook-form with zod, Tailwind, cookie-parser and express-rate-limit. There is no database, state library or extra layers.
evidence.maintainability: There is no README, docs, ADR, spec or staff manual. STAFF_PASSWORD and TRUST_PROXY are documented only by a console.warn and the code. There is no CI configuration. Dependencies use caret ranges with a package-lock. The runtime is set only as engines '>=22', with no .nvmrc. Version 1.0.0 is in package.json, but there is no changelog or release approach. Build/test/lint/typecheck scripts exist and the test suite is a good regression net. Build output (dist/) and agent artifacts (.playwright-mcp/) were delivered in the folder despite being gitignored.

strengths: Every brief requirement is implemented exactly, with server-side seat enforcement in one synchronous step (no overbooking) and field-level error messages shared between client and server through one zod schema.

Solid staff auth: timing-safe digest comparison, random server-side sessions with expiry and sign-out invalidation, HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookies, rate-limited sign-in, and sign-in disabled when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset.
Meaningful API and UI tests covering boundaries, invalid input, cancellation freeing seats, session expiry and accessible error descriptions, inside a small, clean, well-structured codebase.
issues: No README, docs or CI: setup, the STAFF_PASSWORD/TRUST_PROXY variables and staff usage are undocumented, and dist/ plus .playwright-mcp/ artifacts were delivered in the folder.
Staff 'Cancel' deletes immediately with no confirmation, and all Cancel buttons share one accessible name; a staff list load error renders an empty page silently.
Server field errors (for example 'Only 4 seats left') are not focused or announced, the seats-left count on the form goes stale after a 409, and there are no security headers or CSP.
review.verdict: This is a correct, secure and tidy implementation that meets every requirement in the brief, with a pleasant winery look on both desktop and phone and a strong automated test suite. It is close to shippable, but the missing README, CI and staff documentation, plus a few small UX and accessibility gaps around cancelling bookings and server error feedback, should be fixed first.
